# TCP animated episodes

The founder as an animated character, in short comedy episodes that teach one idea, for TikTok. Each
episode follows the master brief (v1.2): entertainment, then the idea, then TCP, then one ask. Every
episode is made twice from one master: once for the TCP account and once for the founder's own.

**How they're made.** The character is drawn in code (`brand/source/reels/toon/`), not generated by
an AI image or video model. He's a detailed 2D cartoon: inked outlines, shading from the screen's
light, and the founder's own proportions, taken from his photos and drawn as a true three-quarter
view. His six-panel cap, the collar of his black AMIRI crewneck and his pearl chain are small 3D
models turned to the same angle as his face, so the brim, seams, eyelets and crown logo sit in true
perspective and the chain drapes round his neck and down his chest; the same models give the cap
worn backwards and the view from behind. His hair is cut short under the cap. He's built strong:
a thick neck, round shoulders, a deep chest narrowing to the waist. Each arm is a shoulder, elbow and
wrist placed as it would really be seen from that angle, with the sleeve following the muscle under
it, so his arms keep their length in every pose. His hands are drawn from their bones to real
proportions (tapered fingers, knuckle creases, nails), so they hold the mouse, the keyboard and the
phone properly; in the phone shot his hand holds it as he would see it himself. The AMIRI wordmark
wraps round his chest and stays readable when he faces the other way. His face, cap, chain and
clothes are built from fixed shapes, so they can't drift between shots. Episodes are scripts in `brand/source/reels/specs/`, rendered by the reel
studio like the other reels. Charts in the stories are examples, labelled on screen. App footage is
the real Quant Terminal in demo mode, labelled DEMO PRICES.

**Files for each episode** (1080 × 1920, 30 fps):

| File | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `tcp-<episode>-music.mp4` | The TCP account, with TCP's own music and sound effects |
| `tcp-<episode>-sfx.mp4` | The sound effects only. Add a trending sound in TikTok and keep the original sound at about 50% |
| `tcp-<episode>-personal-music.mp4`, `-personal-sfx.mp4` | The same two, cut for the founder's account |
| `tcp-<episode>-cover.jpg`, `-personal-cover.jpg` | The cover frames |

**The character sheet** (`tcp-founder-character-sheet.png`, V6) is the canonical look: Lewis approved
it on 5 October 2026. Changes to his face or clothes happen only when a script calls for them.

## EP02 · Every Trader Has Done This

### A. Episode card

| | |
|---|---|
| Title | Every Trader Has Done This |
| Pillar | Trading comedy, with one lesson |
| Length | 26.6 s |
| Accounts | TCP (`tcp-ep02-every-trader-*`) and personal (`tcp-ep02-every-trader-personal-*`) |
| The idea | Wait for the trap, then the structure, then the pullback |
| Ask | TCP: *Follow TCP*. Personal: *Follow for the next one* |

The brief's ask for this episode was "follow / free community". It's follow only: joining the Inner
Circle needs a broker account through the partner link, so calling it free would mislead, and asking
TikTok viewers to open a CFD account is a regulated promotion in the UK. The link in bio and the bot
handle joining, with the disclosures.

### B. Hook options

Ranked by how different the mechanism is, not by how well they'd do.

1. **"just one more breakout…"** (used). Self-recognition: the viewer hears their own inner voice
   before anything happens, and stays to see it go wrong.
2. **"every trader has done this"** (the TCP cut's line above it). A challenge: viewers want to see
   whether they have, and the comments fill with "not me" and tags.
3. **"POV: you called it a fakeout"**. The POV format puts the viewer in the chair, and "fakeout"
   is a word they'll want explained.

### E. Character continuity

- **Outfit, every shot:** black cap worn forward with the gold TCP crown, the pearl chain, a black
  crewneck. No shades in this episode.
- **Expressions:** urgent (brows down, lids narrow) at the screen; frozen, then the side-eye to
  camera (shot 6); disbelief (eyes wide, brows up, mouth open) in shot 10; tired and thinking in shot
  11; a small smirk in shot 13. He never grins.
- **Pose:** right hand on the mouse and left hand on the keyboard until shot 11; arms folded from
  shot 11.
- **Props:** monitor, keyboard, mouse, a black mug with the crown, his phone.
- **Continuity:** one pose track and one chart track run under every shot, so a cut never changes
  what he's doing or where the price is.

### F. Environment

- **Where:** his desk at home, at night. A window behind him with the city lit up; a framed TCP print
  on the wall; a warm gold light strip behind the desk.
- **Light:** the monitor is the key light, cool on his face. It turns red when a big red candle
  prints and green on the rip, so the chart's moves land on his face. Warm gold from behind.
- **Colour:** black and warm gold, cool screen light. Red and green only come from the chart.
- **Background action:** none. No other people.

### G. Animation

The tool is the reel studio. `brand/source/reels/specs/ep02-every-trader.js` is the whole episode:
each shot is one line (set, start, end, camera keys), the founder's poses are one list of keys, and
the chart's progress is another. To change a moment, change its line and render again:

```sh
node render.cjs ep02-every-trader $W --stills=4.3,9.5      # check a moment
node render.cjs ep02-every-trader $W                        # the TCP cut
node render.cjs ep02-every-trader $W --variant=personal     # the founder's cut
```

The sets are in `toon/toon.js` (`desk`, `ots`, `screen`, `mouse`) and the character in
`toon/founder.js`. Continuity rules for any change: no new clothes or jewellery, the crown always on
the cap's front, five fingers on every visible hand, and chart text that is real and readable.

### H. Product

- **19.8–23.8:** the real Quant Terminal on his phone, held in his hand: the Markets tab, scrolling
  from the price and the engine briefing to the 15-minute chart with the previous day's high and low
  and the Asia range drawn on. It's footage of the app itself (`capture.cjs`, shot `markets`), in
  demo mode, labelled DEMO PRICES above the phone.
- **The end card** names it: *The Quant Terminal, inside Telegram.*
- Nothing else in the episode is product: the chart on his monitor is a story chart, labelled
  EXAMPLE CHART · NOT REAL PRICES.

### I. Edit map

- **Tempo:** cuts sit on a 120 bpm grid (a beat is 0.5 s): 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.6, 6.0, 7.0, 8.9 (the
  rip's stop-out leads it), 10.0, 12.0, 18.4, 19.8, 23.8.
- **Music** (the `-music` cut): in from the first frame, out at 4.34 and 8.64 for the punchlines,
  back at 6.0 and 10.0. With a trending sound, use the `-sfx` cut and let the sound's own drop land
  near 4.3 if it can.
- **Text:** one thought at a time, popping in on the beat. Lesson notes at 13.9, 15.1 and 16.3, each
  held 1.2 s.
- **Zooms:** slow push-ins on every shot; the stop-outs get a 0.45 s shake and a red edge.
- **Speed:** the replay rewinds 15 candles in 0.5 s, plays the trades back in 1 s, then slows to a
  candle every 0.4 s for the lesson.
- **Effects:** clicks at 3.15 and 7.15; slams at 4.3 and 8.6; whoosh at 12.12; pops at 13.9, 15.1
  and 16.3; a rise at 17.0; a whoosh into the end card.

### L. QA

- **Narrative:** the joke works without sound; each beat is one shot; the lesson comes from the
  story (his two losses *are* the trap).
- **Visual:** one drawing of him in every shot; five fingers on every hand; no warped screens; chart
  and app text is real and readable; no floating objects (the phone is in his hand); no neon "AI
  trader" look.
- **Trading:** one idea; no statistics; the chart says it's an example; no profit claims; no luxury
  shots.
- **Product:** the app footage is the real app, labelled demo; what the caption says it does (draw
  the levels) is what it does.
- **Brand:** the crown on his cap, on the wall print and on his mug; gold only as an accent; one ask.
- **Platform:** text clear of TikTok's buttons and caption area (checked with `--safe`); readable at
  phone size; works muted.
- **Labels:** no AI voice and no AI-generated imagery, so TikTok's AI label isn't needed. Add it if
  in doubt; it costs nothing.

### M. Cover

The opening close-up at 0.9 s: his eyes on the screen and *just one more breakout…* (the TCP cut adds
EVERY TRADER HAS DONE THIS above it). If TikTok asks for cover text, use *every trader has done this*.

### N. Caption and hashtags

In J and K. Keep the risk line last.

### O. Production split

- **Made here:** script, character, sets, animation, chart, captions, music and effects, both cuts,
  covers, captions for posting.
- **You:** choose a trending sound if you want one (use the `-sfx` file); post each cut to its
  account at the times in P; tell me what the comments say.

### P. Posting

UK times. The two accounts post a day apart, so the same story never goes out twice in one day.

| When | Account | File | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mon 5 Oct, 19:30 | TCP | `tcp-ep02-every-trader-music.mp4` | TikTok, caption K |
| Mon 5 Oct, 20:00 | TCP | the same file | Instagram Reels, caption K |
| Tue 6 Oct, 19:30 | Founder | `tcp-ep02-every-trader-personal-music.mp4` | TikTok, caption J |
| Tue 6 Oct, 20:00 | Founder | the same file | Instagram Reels, caption J |

- **Cover:** the frame at 0.9 s (`-cover.jpg`); if TikTok asks for cover text, *every trader has done
  this*.
- **Pin** it to the founder's profile; on TCP's, it joins the three pins in `POSTS.md` once batch 1 is
  up.
- **No AI label needed:** no AI voice and no AI imagery. With a trending sound, use the `-sfx` file
  and keep the original sound at about 50%.
- **The first hour:** answer the early comments, ideally with a short video reply; TikTok pushes
  replies. Note the three-second hold rate after a day.
